title: Gin Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Send a text reply
examples.description: GET /hello calls this handler. Context.String sends formatted text with a status.

examples.title: Send a JSON object
examples.description: gin.H is a short map type for named data. Open GET /book.

examples.title: Read a path parameter
examples.description: A colon marks a route value. GET /hello/Ravi puts Ravi in the name parameter.

examples.title: Read a query value
examples.description: DefaultQuery reads a query parameter and supplies a fallback. GET /page uses the text fallback 1.

examples.title: Parse a number
examples.description: strconv.Atoi turns text into an int or reports an error. Open GET /double/4.

examples.title: Read a JSON body
examples.description: ShouldBindJSON reads and checks JSON fields. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}.

examples.title: Share a route prefix
examples.description: A group gives related handlers a common path prefix. Open GET /api/books.

examples.title: Run a shared request step
examples.description: Middleware can set request values before calling the next handler. Open GET /school.

examples.title: Add response metadata
examples.description: Header sets a response header. Open GET /note and inspect Cache-Control.

examples.title: Return a redirect
examples.description: Redirect asks the client to visit a new URL. GET /start ends at /hello in a browser.

examples.title: Handle unmatched routes
examples.description: NoRoute supplies a fallback handler. GET /missing has no normal route.

examples.title: Stop a handler chain
examples.description: AbortWithStatusJSON stops later handlers in the chain. GET /closed receives this practice block message.
